findings.title: CSP unsafe-eval gated only by NODE_ENV
findings.desc: `allowUnsafeEval` defaults to `process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"`, so any deployment where NODE_ENV isn't explicitly set to `"production"` (e.g. staging, misconfigured containers, `NODE_ENV=test`) will silently ship `'unsafe-eval'` in the CSP, weakening XSS mitigation without any explicit opt-in at the call site.

findings.title: Partial `between` tuple can still render `undefined`
findings.desc: The new guard only checks `t.between` truthiness; if streaming yields a one-element array (e.g. `["A"]`), `t.between[1]` will render as literal `undefined` text inside the `<span>`, which is a residual edge case of the same partial-streaming problem being fixed.

findings.title: CSP eval relaxation keyed off ambient NODE_ENV
findings.desc: `buildCsp` defaults `allowUnsafeEval` to `process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"`, so any deployment/staging environment that doesn't explicitly set `NODE_ENV=production` (e.g. a misconfigured preview/staging build) will silently ship `'unsafe-eval'` in the CSP. This is a meaningful security regression path even though it's documented as intentional for local dev.

findings.title: Tension.between typed as required but is optional at runtime
findings.desc: The fix correctly guards against `t.between` being `undefined` during streaming, but the underlying `Tension` type (`between: [string, string]`) still declares it as always present, so the type system doesn't reflect real runtime behavior — future code touching `tensions` elsewhere can reintroduce the same crash without a type error warning them.

findings.title: CSP 'unsafe-eval' gated only by NODE_ENV
findings.desc: `allowUnsafeEval` defaults to `true` whenever `NODE_ENV !== "production"` (e.g. `"staging"`, `"test"`, or unset), so any non-production deployment that doesn't set `NODE_ENV` to exactly `"production"` will silently serve `'unsafe-eval'` in its CSP to real users, weakening XSS mitigations without an explicit opt-in.
